transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held. Airlines are working to get a backlog
of passengers back up in planes after Friday's nationwide ground stop to fix outdated technology
Trump administration officials say it's up to Congress to approve more money. NPR's
Mara Liasson reports.
Speaking to reporters yesterday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communication systems
work by a contractor was the culprit, not new AI tools or a cyber attack.
"We don't believe this was cyber at all. This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment."
Duffy blamed Congress for not giving the FAA more money for upgrades, but Republicans who
are still in charge of Congress until January already approved $12.5 billion for safety
upgrades in the One Big Beautiful bill. Democrats on the House Transportation and Infrastructure
Committee say that the administration has only spent $1 billion of those funds. Mara
Liasson, NPR News.
The Port of New Orleans has sued the owners of the tanker that collided with a docked
cruise ship for $1 million, NPR's Ava Pukach reports.
The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans lawsuit says the collision occurred
as a result of gross negligence by tanker Atlantic Asphalt and its owner in management
company. A federal judge approved the port official's request to have the tanker seized.
John DeLoof, the National Transportation Safety Board, says the tanker's voyage data recorder
was recovered.
"So it's like a flight data recorder on an aircraft where we can look at speeds and all
kinds of information."
City officials say it could be weeks before the American Heritage cruise ship is fully
removed from the site. The Coast Guard is assisting with removal of hazardous material
on board. Ava Pukach, NPR News.
A federal judge has temporarily blocked President Trump's plans to redevelop a public park and
golf course in Washington, D.C., NPR's Kate Bartlett reports.
The judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work on the site, which had been due
to close on Sunday for 15 months while it was redeveloped. Trump, an avid golfer, wants
to turn the historic site, East Potomac Golf Links, into a championship-level golf course.
The plaintiffs in the case, including the D.C. Preservation League, argue the new course
would be unaffordable. On Saturday, before the order, Trump said on social media that
anyone in the D.C. area would be given a 50 percent discount.
The development is just one of the president's planned projects in the nation's capital,
Kate Bartlett, NPR News.
The vote count in Alaska goes on for the U.S. Senate race, and the latest tally shows Democratic
Representative Mary Peltola now leads Republican Senator Dan Sullivan with 49.9 percent of
the vote. Any candidate who reaches 50 percent once all the votes are in wins. Otherwise,
there's a runoff. Alaska allows absentee ballots to arrive 15 days after Election Day.
That's Wednesday.
This is NPR News.
MegaSpeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company, said today Alice Huang officially
left the company in August 2025. The New York Times reported the suspected Chinese spy had
an affair with then-Invidia CEO Jensen Huang, and the two companies had business ties. Jensen
Huang has stepped down from Invidia, the company he founded and led that has propelled the
AI revolution.
Italy is finding tech giant Meta nearly $900 million for accessing Facebook users' photos
and videos stored on Android devices. Esme Nicholson reports.
Italy's data protection agency says Meta has violated European privacy directives by
failing to obtain specific consent and to properly inform users that its Facebook app
could access all photos and videos and the related metadata on Android devices. The regulator
says Facebook's access permissions were not transparent and users did not understand what
they were authorizing. It has instructed Meta to seek consent with separate, specific and
clear requests. The authority also cited Meta's lack of cooperation during the investigation.
The fine comes to about 0.4 percent of Meta's annual turnover.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
Southeast Asian leaders have opened their annual summit in Manila for three days of
talks. Members will discuss world conflicts, including in Myanmar. Today, they issued a
rebuke to the military-backed regime for failing to comply with a peace plan. President Trump
is due to arrive on Tuesday.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: FAA communications system outage prompts airline backlogs; Duffy blames Congress for underfunding upgrades
Port of New Orleans sues tanker Atlantic Asphalt owners for $1 million after cruise ship collision
Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump redevelopment of East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C.
Alaska Senate race vote count shows Mary Peltola leading Dan Sullivan at 49.9 percent
Alice Huang, suspected Chinese spy, left MegaSpeed in August 2025, company confirms
Italy fines Meta nearly $900 million over Android photo and video access without consent
Southeast Asian leaders open annual summit in Manila, rebuke Myanmar military regime over peace plan
